ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure is an asymptotic amplitude-frequency Bode plot, with the vertical axis as |G(ω)| in dB and the horizontal axis as log ω. The slope of the curve in the low-frequency band is labeled -20 dB/decade; at ω1 the curve becomes a horizontal line, with slope 0; at ω2 the curve bends again, and after that the slope is labeled -40 dB/decade. Reasoning: The transfer function is G(s)=k(s+z)^a/[s^b(s+p)^c]. The origin pole factor s^b is in the denominator, making the initial low-frequency slope -20b dB/decade. The initial slope in the figure is -20 dB/decade, so b=1. At ω1 the slope changes from -20 to 0, with a change of +20 dB/decade, corresponding to one finite zero, therefore a=1. At ω2 the slope changes from 0 to -40, with a change of -40 dB/decade, corresponding to two finite poles, therefore c=2. Therefore a+b+c=1+1+2=4.

method.method_draft: From the initial slope -20 dB/decade, infer b=1 because the factor s^b in the denominator gives -20b dB/decade. At omega_1 the slope changes from -20 to 0, a +20 dB/decade change, so the numerator finite zero order is a=1. At omega_2 the slope changes from 0 to -40, a -40 dB/decade change, so the finite pole order is c=2. Therefore compute a+b+c=1+1+2=4.
